title: Juicy Fermented Greek Turkey Neck Dolmades
description: A pescatarian-friendly Greek dish featuring turkey neck, served in a fermented and juicy dolmade form, perfect for crowds. This recipe combines the flavors of Greece with the tenderness of turkey neck.
instructions: Rinse the turkey necks and place them in a large pot with the water, white wine, salt, and black pepper.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat and let it simmer for 2 hours, or until the turkey is tender.
Remove the turkey from the pot and let it cool, then shred it into bite-sized pieces.
Meanwhile, prepare the grape leaves by blanching them in boiling water for 30 seconds, then rinsing them in cold water.
In a large bowl, combine the shredded turkey, olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, and chopped fresh dill.
Layout a grape leaf on a flat surface, with the stem end facing you, and place about 1 tablespoon of the turkey mixture in the center of the leaf.
Fold the stem end over the filling, then fold in the sides and roll the leaf into a neat package.
Repeat with the remaining grape leaves and turkey mixture.
Place the dolmades in a large serving dish, seam-side down, and serve.
Let the dolmades ferment at room temperature for at least 24 hours before serving.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
